ocr_text: PREFACE ANGOON UNIVERSITY, in starting on the work of publishing facsimiles of the inscriptions of Burma, is following the good example set by the French Academie des Inscriptions et Belles Lettres, which since 1926' has been doing the same for the inscriptions of Camboja. It is not necessary to lay stress on the importance of these inscriptions; they are the main source of our knowledge of the older history of these countries; they are also the first extant specimens of their language and literature. All must sooner or later be edited, with full annotation and translation. But it will be long before this labour is completed; and meantime there seems to be no reason to delays published books containing the text of the inscription or its translation into English, (c) the original reader will find the same plate-number and a brief identification of the inscription in Burmese.
notes: Front matter states that the volume publishes facsimiles and points readers to books containing text or English translation.
